newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Taiwan Strait links little impact on HK -StanChart.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Strait links little impact on HK -StanChart.

text.p: Standard Chartered Bank said on Thursday direct shipping links between China and Taiwan would have little impact on Hong Kong's trade.

On Wednesday Taiwan's transport ministry said a Hong Kong-owned container ship had arrived at the port of Kaohsiung on February 23 from China's southeastern special economic zone of Xiamen -- the first quasi-direct China-Taiwan passage in nearly 50 years.
Taipei had banned direct links with the mainland since the end of the communist-nationalist Chinese civil war in 1949.

In its February "Greater China Viewpoints" report, Standard Chartered said the opening of the Kaoshiung-Xiamen and Kaoshiung-Fuzhou shipping routes may divert some of the transhipment trade currently handled by Hong Kong to Kaoshiung in the future.
However, the report said the trade that would be affected was estimated to be small, as Xiamen and Fuzhou were relatively small ports.
It said if direct cross-strait trade was allowed, the impact on Hong Kong would be greater, but Hong Kong's status as a major trading centre would not change.

"In any case, as and when the political and economic links across the Taiwan Strait improves, Hong Kong should also benefit from the more prosperous economies of the mainland and Taiwan as the flow in investment, goods and people across the Strait increases," the report said.
The bank also said new trading opportunities would emerge as Hong Kong was well positioned to benefit from the growth in trade between China's mid-west and the outside world.
It said Hong Kong was geographically more convenient than most other Chinese ports and the commissioning of the Beijing- Kowloon railway would enhance Hong Kong's advantages further.
